mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the post-tightening month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 4.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces corporate investment demand.
regime_hint: rising unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of UNRATE > 4.5% months (empirical test).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of GDPC1 (real private consumption) to INDPRO (industrial production) exceeds 1.10 for two consecutive months, it indicates strong demand growth that precedes a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return in 30 such windows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (housing starts) of at least 5% for three months is a leading indicator of a supply shock, resulting in a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during the shock window (empirical failure).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3.5% for four consecutive months during a non-recessionary regime, it predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as low rates support equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly above the 30-day moving average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 10,000 followed by a rise in UNRATE above 5% signals labor market weakness that precedes a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month by ≥10,000 AND UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in 80% of such events (empirical test).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in RSAFS (real private savings) below INDPRO suggests reduced precautionary saving, which is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as spending is expected to rise.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns during the two months after the signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) unexpectedly exceeds the prior month by more than 0.3% and FEDFUNDS remains unchanged, it predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month by >0.3% AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
regime_hint: inflation surprise in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in 90% of such events (empirical test).
